newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsica bombs hit minister's office, deputy's home.
newsitem.headline: Corsica bombs hit minister's office, deputy's home.

text.p: Four bomb blasts struck the Mediterranean island of Corsica overnight, damaging a town hall, a post office and a politician's holiday home, paramilitary police said on Friday.
No one claimed responsibility, but similar attacks have been blamed on Corsican separatists.

The first explosion, at 9.20 p.m. (1920 GMT), damaged the town hall at Ile Rousse, hitting the office of mayor Pierre Pasquini, who is also junior minister for veterans affairs in the French government. A bomb had exploded at his daughter's villa in August.
An hour later, a small bomb caused slight damage at the post office in Biguglia, near Bastia.
At midnight (2200 GMT), a blast hit the holiday home of parliamentarian Jean-Claude Bonacorsi in the town of Sainte Lucie de Moriani.

Police said a 2.5 kg bomb placed under a car in the old harbour district of Bastia caused extensive damage shortly after midnight. It destroyed the vehicle, owned by a coffee wholesaler, as well as damaging a dozen other parked cars.
Militants have waged a low-level guerrilla war for two decades for greater autonomy from mainland France.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decreed a crackdown on separatist violence, but nationalist leaders have accused him of burying secret talks aimed at resolving their differences.
